{{recipe}}

'''Shashlik''' (Russian шашлык from Turkic ''shishlik'' < ''shish'' "rod, skewer") is a dish of usually mostly meat roasted over open fire on [[Cookbook:Skewer|skewers]]. Russians seem to have borrowed making shashliks from peoples of Caucasus mountains, and shashliks have become a picnic/garden party food in Russia similar to barbecue elsewhere. Meat is often specially marinated before roasting, and while in the Caucasus mutton is most common and Muslim peoples may abstain from alcohol, it is not so in Russian culture. Food stores in Russia in the warm season sell equipment for shashliks, like iron ''mangal'' boxes on legs to put fire underneath and skewers on top, skewers, bags of charcoal etc. While both men and women eat shashliks, it may be expected of men to be able to make the dish like other mostly meat dishes.
The secret of the shashlik is that the meat should soak in a marinade for at least 3 hours. 
== Ingredients ==
* 1 [[Cookbook:Kilogram|kg]] [[Cookbook:Pork|pork]] shoulder
* 100 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] [[Cookbook:Vodka|vodka]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Honey|honey]]
* 1 tbsp [[Cookbook:Pepper|black pepper]]
* 1 tbsp prepared [[Cookbook:Mustard|mustard]]
* Pieces of [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], red or green [[Cookbook:Bell Pepper|bell pepper]], [[Cookbook:Bacon|bacon]], [[Cookbook:Sausage|sausage]], [[Cookbook:Cucumber|cucumber]], baby [[Cookbook:Mushroom|mushrooms]]

== Procedure ==
# Mix the honey, mustard, vodka, salt and pepper in a deep bowl and soak the meat pieces in it. Leave the bowl in the refrigerator for 3 hours.
# Arrange the meat pieces on wooden or metal [[Cookbook:Skewer|skewers]], putting some pieces of bacon, sausage, pepper, onion, mushrooms, cucumber, according to your preference, between the pieces of meat.
# [[Cookbook:Grilling|Grill]] the skewers. 
# Serve with potato and other salads! Enjoy!
